prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form that made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my scientific judgment is unchanged, and I keep the argument separate from the fact that all six of us began in the same place. B003 is a continuous discovery arc: Holst on the secretion, actions and degradation of GLP-1, Drucker on proglucagon-derived peptide biology, receptor action and the therapeutic concept, and Mojsov on the identity and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide. It leads through DPP-4 biology to drugs with independently replicated outcome-trial evidence in glycaemic control, weight, and cardiovascular and renal endpoints. No one raised a maturity concern in round 1, and I regard the timing as appropriate. The discovery-anchored trio fits the three-person limit without splitting a coherent contribution, and the citation is worded around the physiology and the active form of the peptide, not around any specific drug.
statement.case_against: The weakness remains credit, not merit. The priority question for the active peptide between Mojsov and the Habener group, who are outside the supplied names, cannot be settled from this record, and I have not verified it independently. Leaving out Knudsen means the prize honours the discovery layer and not the medicinal chemistry that delivered liraglutide and semaglutide, and a reader could call that arbitrary. Long-term safety of chronic incretin use is still accruing. I also accept that convergence of six members on the same evidence is not independent confirmation, so the attribution caveat should be treated as a real open risk and not as a formality.

responses.point: The chair moved from preferring Knudsen at opening to supporting Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, while still describing Mojsov's weight as contested and asking what citation wording handles the Habener-group question.
responses.response: I welcome his move and agree the third seat is the one question the committee should answer openly. My answer is that a citation worded around the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form credits what Mojsov is documented to have done, identifying and synthesising the active peptide, without claiming that she alone discovered the peptide or its biology. If the committee finds that the documented record does not support even that narrower claim, Drucker, Holst and Knudsen becomes the defensible trio, but then the rationale must be stated and not left as an omission. I do not find that case made on what we have, so I keep Mojsov. I would not decide the seat on prominence or on which names the public associates with semaglutide.

responses.point: Linnarsson keeps B003 as a single part and treats CAR-T and SMN2 antisense as the next clinical alternatives, both new therapeutic modalities with clear clinical effect.
responses.response: I agree with him that CAR-T is the strongest alternative. My reservation is the one I raised in round 1: Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept sits outside the credited set. He says this should not delay a CAR-T prize, and I agree in principle, but a two-part prize that I could only support with a misleading citation is worse than a one-part prize. On SMN2 antisense I still place it below CAR-T, because approval dates only from 2016, durability is still being established, and gene-replacement competitors exist. I have not changed that ordering, though I recognise that the Krainer and Bennett pair is cleaner in attribution than the CAR-T trio.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that B003 should honour discovery of the hormone's actions and the therapeutic concept, treating Knudsen's work as translation, and he disagreed with my ordering of B010 above B043.
responses.response: I agree on Knudsen and on the structure of the prize. On B010 versus B043 I take his point that much of the CML conceptual foundation lies in the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL discoveries outside Druker, Lydon and Sawyers, and I concede that this weakens B010 as a stand-alone prize. I keep it as an alternative because the clinical proof, with two decades of survival data, is mature and not in dispute. I still would not put B043 ahead of it, since the PERK and ATF6 arms (Ron, Harding, Kaufman) are missing and disease relevance has not been shown at the same level. This is a difference of weighting, and I will not press it into a ruling.

responses.point: El Manira holds optogenetics (B036) as the leading second candidate, a transformative causal tool, while acknowledging that the three-person cap leaves out decisive contributors.
responses.response: I agree that optogenetics changed how causal questions are asked in neuroscience. What I cannot do is find a trio of the six credited names that does not exclude someone with a decisive claim, whether Hegemann, Bamberg or Miesenboeck, and I weigh a method below a disease-level advance for this year. His own concession on the cap is the reason I would not add a second part for it now. I think B036 is a serious candidate for a later year if the committee is prepared to define a discovery-focused credit, but his argument has not changed my configuration.

uncertainties: Whether the documented record supports Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide as distinct from the Habener-group work, which I cannot resolve from the supplied names.
Whether the committee will accept a one-part prize that leaves out Knudsen, with an explicit rationale that her contribution was development and not discovery.
Whether CAR-T could be supported as a second part without a citation that misstates the origin of the chimeric receptor concept, given Eshhar's absence.
Long-term safety of chronic incretin use is still accruing.
statement.conflict_note: Updated: no documented personal tie to Drucker, Holst, Mojsov or Knudsen, and none that would call for recusal on B003. TNF blockade (B016) falls in my clinical field of rheumatology; it has not become a serious contender, but I would flag it if it did. B015 and B010 are named only as alternatives, and I have no documented tie to their credited names.
